title: The Red Line
synopsis: Three women fall prey to a ruthless phone scam. To settle the score, they'll take on the criminal network that stole their money and their dignity.
reviews: 4/10 Unfortunately, I gave up the show at around 1 hour mark. The plot is simply too unrealistic, and this really gives no good emotion to watch the show. You can say that movie is movie, it will never be 100% real. But given the fact this script is inspired by reality world scams, it should not be farfetched this way. I can list a few, 1. What would motivate the trio to go as far as investigating the whole scam on their own. They only lost like 500k-1 million baht not 10 million. Furthermore, no lives involved. And not to mention they are generally quite well to do. Why would they bother.2. There are no scammers that would meet a victim in real life. 3. There are no scammers that use their real face in a video call. 4. There are no scammers that would operate so locally. E.g. Operate in Bangkok and scam in Bangkok...come on. 5. You can't really leave a real syndicate tat easily. The boss and Yui just left like it was a regular job lol, and opened their own scam company. Bahhh.

7/10 A great revenge style thriller I enjoyed this film more than I thought I would. There has been a story similer to this on netflix before and I think this one might have something above that. In this movie three very different woman, Mother orn, physical therapist fai and wawwo, whos grandma got scammed along with herself bound together to track down the scammers responsible for stealing a whole lot of money from them. Its great to watch the in which they do it and its clever in places and well acted. Overall I enjoyed it.

3/10 Strong start but end up a failure The topic of call center scams is very popular among Thai audiences, so I was confident this movie would be entertaining. The first 30 minutes were captivating and full of tension. Most of the actors delivered strong performances, and the color grading was beautiful, helping to set the mood and tone effectively. However, things gradually start to fall apart as the story progresses. The plot becomes increasingly illogical, and the call center gang is portrayed as so careless that it becomes ridiculous. The protagonists end up winning through pure coincidence rather than skill, which makes their victory feel unearned and not even satisfying. The ending was especially disappointing. In one scene near the end, the female lead argues with the antagonist, who is pointing a gun at her, about who has already lost. It felt completely unrealistic and almost laughable. At the very end, it seems the female lead decides to go to Poipet to take down a larger call center gang. This is supposed to be a serious and emotional moment, but it lacks impact. Just minutes earlier, she apologized to her daughter for neglecting her and told her husband to take better care of their child. Yet she then abandons them to pursue this mission alone. Where is her sense of responsibility as a parent? I might have accepted this if the movie were a fantasy or a comedy, but it presents itself as a thriller based on real-life issues. Because of that, I can't recommend it. It's not worth your time.

4/10 Man, the plot is a mess. So many loopholes everywhere. And the ending? Makes zero sense why they'd do that. It honestly reminds me of Squid Game Season 2 the main character is kinda dumb but tries to act like a hero, dragging everyone around him down with him. He only survives because of pure luck. Same thing here. Trying to get revenge with that last minute move at the end it just doesn't make any sense at all. Some characters feel completely pointless, like... why are they even there? No substance whatsoever. Like the cop totally reminds me of the cop in Squid Game Season 3.

8/10 Slow at first but surpassed by expectations. It's not a bad movie as some claimed although its not suitable for all audience. It requires waiting on and understanding the characters more and their motives and it gets quite good and interesting and good thriller with good movie acting overall worth watching and it shares good important security lessons

2/10 Out of reality The story is interesting, about con artists and their victims. However, the entire narrative and development of the three victims' espionage against the gang was very fantastical and disjointed. The girl falling from the building and only breaking two fingernails was ridiculous. Everyone in this film was always sweaty and dirty-looking, conveying the image that all poor people are dirty and unhygienic. The acting of the entire cast is terrible and irritatingly caricatured. The explicit sex scene, around the first 50 minutes, was completely unnecessary to the plot; and this vulgar appeal influenced my rating of 2.

7/10 Decent film.Running time needed to be shorter,good cinematography.Recommended.Watch with subs in original.Nice to see other cultures believes in supernatural world.

7/10 I must say I put my expectation high for this since I love Binjong's previous movies. Alone and Shutter but I'm a bit not satisfied since this one is less scary and story is less impacted compare to his previous horror work. Most scariest scene are already in the trailer and some part doesn't really make sense and brought more question than answer. Thai-Korean supernatural horror, Banjong Pisanthanakun's 'The Medium,' burns slowly but intensely throughout. It has all the elements of Asian horror unique to the Korean and Thai genres, such as creepy music and a darkly saturated filter. The film loses steam at times owing to flaws in its mockumentary style, but Pisanthanakun succeeds far more when he concentrates on the complexities of the familial links and what some of the key reveals imply for each character.

In the first leg it has a lot going for it. The cinematography is great, and as much as they attempt to make things dreary, this thing could really function as travel vlog for Thailand. The faux doc style brings a realism to the mystic elements and it feels like a unique backdrop for a horror flick. The setup is slow but enjoyable and you begin to wonder if it's ever going to erupt into full blown horror. Rest assured, it does. However, with the quality of the preamble, you grow to believe the film had something more clever up it's sleeve. What you eventually get is a rather run of the mill possession tale, and things sort of fall apart from there.Where the mocumentary initially lent credibility, it eventually devolves into the common found footage problem of "why would a real cameraman actually be filming this?" At one point reaching the height of ridiculousness where a girl has a mishap with her period and the camera follows her to the bathroom, like a psychopath. The possession element does little to set itself apart from it's many contemporaries, aside from forgoing the regular Christian/Satan angle. Narilya Gulmongkolpech's performance is enthusiastic but is often reminiscent of haunted house staff doing the crazy/scary routine. The whole thing seems to overstay it's welcome a bit, which is strange because the slow build seems to breeze by and it's only when things heat up that they start to feel redundant.I don't want to be too hard on it, because it's in many ways a well made picture, it just doesn't live up to it's own potential.

The Medium begins as a captivating yet slow-burning thriller that eventually transitions into recycled scares and an incredibly underwhelming finish. If you've watched horror films centred around spiritual possession, then you have a good idea of what to expect. The Medium does not try to do anything new with the formula as it boldly embraces every found footage cliché. In addition, the actions of some characters will definitely frustrate and seem like cheap ways to move the plot closer to its chaotic yet uninspired climax. I'd recommend watching The Wailing and skipping this one.

Saw this at the cinema last night, and while I found it to be good-looking and well-made, with an interesting setting, it was still nothing new or special. I've seen everything in this film before. Nowhere near on the same level as The Wailing, which this shares many elements with.The screaming and running around and people acting possessed in the last act becomes tedious after a while, as there's barely any emotional involvement with the characters. I simply did not care about any of the characters who made it to the last act.Not often I'd say this about a horror film, but this would have been improved by actually being subtler, and leaving out some of the mayhem. And an edit - this is much too long at 130mins.

This was suprisingly good until the characters got completely stupid. There was some great creativity in the plot, but like so many movies, the writers relied on utter stupidity from the characters to drive the plot and situations forward. Some great scenes in this film though. Very hardcore in some aspects.

The Thai horror has just achieved a new step up into the genre with this bone-chilling, nerve-wracking movie. Its more than two hours fly through a complex and engaging story revolving about family, legacy, curses and devilish fates. It's more fast paced and much more entertaining than many movies under 90 minutes. The performances are top notch and the filmmaking style a la found footage is very effective. The POV helps to introduce the audience into the reality of the story, so when the scares starts, it's a total knock-out. Until a more conventional third act (in a good way, though), the two thirds of the movie manages to scare the living daylights of you without cheap jump-scares, which is pure gold nowadays. The ending is much more filled with them, but that's not a downer for me at all. It's a twisted, ballsy ending that works wonderfully with how the story was building up until that moment. While I could watch it with lights out (unlike the Thai cinemas whose audience demanded to watch it with lights on - if it is not a marketing sting), I recognize its hipnotic power upon me from start to finish, its ability to scare properly and the fact that I keep thinking about the movie after watching it. A terrific horror movie, a must see if you are a fan of the genre.

The scariest film of the year so far and one of the creepiest entries in the world of horror in recent years, The Medium begins as a documentary about a shaman possessed by a local deity in North-east Thailand but soon develops into a dreadful & diabolical nightmare that you can't escape from. Powerful, petrifying & perturbing in equal measure, this Thai-South Korean supernatural horror reeks of death & devilry.Co-written by Na Hong-jin (The Wailing) & directed by Banjong Pisanthanakun (Shutter), the film employs the faux-documentary format to narrate its tale of faith, inheritance, malaise & malison and gradually brings the viewers into its world of beliefs, curses & superstitions with its informative approach & natural acting from the cast. It takes its time, is never in a hurry & starts to ratchet things up only after the audience is fully on board.While suffused with a feeling of something sinister & unholy brewing under the surface from the beginning, the film's horror elements lunges to the forefront only after the board is set & all the characters are properly introduced. And the execution is genuinely effective & nerve-wracking. There are scenes in here that are downright shocking & disturbing but what lends those moments their uncanny weight & power are the thoroughly convincing performances.Overall, The Medium is one of those unnerving horror offerings that feels cursed, brims with an ill-omened quality and is smeared with a blood-curdling atmosphere that only intensifies as plot progresses. Intelligently directed, deftly scripted, finely detailed & strongly bolstered by Narilya Gulmongkolpech's bone-chilling act, the film does run longer than it needs to but the terror it invokes from its eerie setting & skin-crawling imagery is as unrelenting as it is unsettling. Don't miss it.

Unsatisfactory at freaking all. And also, the character. How are you so freaking dumb to live with possessed people in a same house, let alone with a freaking baby? I haven't watched anything so EERIE/Unsettling is a long time. Something I dislike about horror movies is that they take the easy way out and heavily on jump scares and I am not a fan of that. If you can make a horror movie that's creepy, you have my money. The Medium was just that. I counted, and there ONE jump-scare in this one.The movie talks about Shamanism in Thailand, so there's a little bit you'll learn about the culture. The movie was very well shot too! PHENOMENAL acting by everyone involved, especially the lead. The film did NOT hold back and went all out. Two particular 'shocking/horrific' scenes in the movie make it not for the squeamish. Nobody/nothing is off limits. But if you're the "I like me some Horror" types, you HAVE to watch this.The storytelling is...not straightforward. Is that a flaw? Maybe/maybe not. It's also a slow-burn, you'll have to be a little patient. I had VARIOUS questions after the movie, which I had to look up and read to find answers for. But questions kept aside, you should watch it just for the creeps. If you then want to chat about the movie, this is for you!

Probably the best found footage ever and one of the best possession films in history.Sad that this short attention span world (affecting already order generations, of course, due to the usage of the same tools the young use) will never recognise this as the classic it should be.
This was a slow burner and some people might not have patience to stay til end. Trust me stick with it , there are some really frightening scenes especially in last third of movie.

At least 40 minutes too long with a terrible ending.By the end of the movie everyone behaves like they've never had a brain in their head. They all deserve what happened to them in the end for being so dumb.

Spoiler Free: This movie has been on my watchlist and I was so happy when it finally came out! I saw some mixed reviews and while I can understand, I sit here purely and utterly terrified. I didn't expect the movie to be other than a medicore and low budget horror coming from Thailand but it remided me of the pov the blairwitch project and the mix documentary style story telling made it more impactful.The locations stylish choice of narration made it a unique flim to watch after a long time

The first two-thirds of The Medium are surprisingly brilliant-bordering on a true masterpiece. It provides a deep, immersive look into the nuances of spirituality and folk belief. Initially, the film adopts a documentary-style realism that makes you feel like an active and intimate witness to the unfolding events. It is fascinating to observe the slow, unconscious "spiritual decay" of the protagonist as she begins to lose her grip on her own soul, a process that is handled with incredible tension and realism for the majority of the film.However, the final act completely derails the experience. Everything becomes unnecessarily chaotic, and the characters-who had been grounded until then-suddenly start making inexplicably poor or foolish decisions, and the initial tension or climax evaporates as the story devolves into a "pseudo-zombie" spectacle that lacks any of the sophistication of the preceding hour and a half. In my opinion, this shift stripped away the haunting "magic" and psychological depth established in the first two acts. It is a genuine shame because the ending effectively erases the brilliance and depth the film worked so hard to build... a 10/10 beginning with a 2/10 ending in my opinion. What a truly disappointing ending!!!

Less is almost always more in horror. Especially in demon/possession films. When people watch 'Paranormal Activity' and say it felt like nothing happened, I tell them that's why it's so effective. It's supernatural, however it feels like it could happen for that reason. 'The Medium' goes the other way. It goes off the wall nuts, and for that reason I found it almost completely ineffective and frankly boring.The film is long - and it feels like it. It's over two hours long and the pacing simply can't justify it. Not many horror movies can to be fair. Also the film is found footage, however it never feels like it. Found footage (or in this case Mockumentary) films usually have a very gritty and real feel to them. You should feel like you are watching something you shouldn't be from the dark depths of the internet. The only thing it really added to this one was some odd camera angles.The biggest problem with this one though is that it is simply not scary. The main possessed girl had no menace and no aesthetically scary aspects about her. Also all the violence felt forced and overdone. I wanted to like this one, but it was a miss for me sadly. 5/10.

Followed by a film crew, the psychic medium of a remote section of Thailand being documented uncovers enough evidence to realize her niece is the target of a supernatural attack and tries to save her, but as it continues finds herself confronted by a darker and more malicious spirit than she anticipated.While there's quite a lot to like, this one does come off as slightly disappointing. Where it is best is the setup, offering the kind of real-world grounding required for a story like this one. Since the initial introduction here is on her abilities and spiritual connection to the Gods of the area and how she treats those who need it, there's a fantastic understanding of how strong her connection to that realm is. By understanding that connection this clearly, the later focus on the family members who are suddenly coming under attack by the various supernatural maladies on the daughter comes into greater focus, from the behavioral shifts ranging from sudden quietness to overtly flirtatious and outgoing, defensive attitudes about strangely impersonal objects and the discomfort felt around the family. Given that all of this is shot like a found-footage effort by the documentary crew following Nim the psychic brings a real-world approach that's not oversensationalized or grandiose which helps the film tremendously. Once the setup is in place, the film provides a lot of fun with the realization that she has to use her powers to help the possessed daughter. Having gathered a series of clues not just from those behavioral changes and outbursts but also much more in the wake of how we're told they came together leading to that conclusion, the tension and action ramp up considerably as her condition has been revealed and the outbursts turn violent including the shower attack or the beatdown with the video camera during a ritual ceremony leading to a far more intense and suspenseful second half. The attempts at using her own powers as a means of controlling and figuring out what's going on have a fine localized flair that involves several rituals and the realization that they've been deceived all along, the race to uncover the truth about what's possessing the daughter and free her from its grasp results in some fascinating ritualistic work. The final exorcism itself, a massive outpouring of dark magic rituals and ceremonial preparations that take place in several fine scenarios throughout here, are chilling and somewhat shocking to witness, making for a highly effective and enjoyable effort. While there's a lot to like, this one does fall short somewhat. Most of them come in the form of an overly complicated story that tries to do more than it should. While the early focus is on grounding the life of everyone in the area so that the terror is that much more palpable, things progress beyond an obvious point that something should be done quite early and often. Several instances with encounters at her work, numerous bizarre videos showing how she interacts with others in the community and all the socially distant behavior around the family are more than enough to suspect something has gone wrong, however, it takes until the physical attacks on the family to even confront her about something going wrong. From there, the revelation about the former boyfriend who died recently haunting her that turns into a red herring for the ancestral curse being the cause of the possession is unnecessary. This explanation comes way too late in the film to mean anything with no build-up following the evidence we've gathered so far, leading to too many plot points and storylines to keep track of than what should be the case. Likewise, there's also the minor issue of this being just a bit too long, running on about ten-to-fifteen minutes longer than necessary with cramming too much into it or running beyond its usefulness in either the drama setup or its horror setpieces. While it all adds to the terror experienced, some of it isn't necessary and could've been taken out, but beyond that, there's not much to dislike here.Rated Unrated/R: Extreme Graphic Violence, Nudity, Language, and a sex scene.

This is a take on demonic possession that I mostly really liked, but there are certainly some things that held The Medium back from greatness while never harming the film so much I wanted to give up on it or fully disengage.It starts slow and heavy on mystery, and not knowing where it was going ended up being a little more interesting than where it went by its final act. It follows a family in Thailand who have inherited - and pass down from generation to generation - a spirit named Ba Yan that grants one family member per generation shaman powers. It's hard for me to describe; I don't know if I'm getting the terminology right. BUT: the film does a great job at explaining it and letting it be straightforward to follow in the moment. You get a handle on all the family members, with the film slowly revealing what's at stake. It can be a little slow, but it really works and feels very intriguing.At around the halfway point, things felt a bit less fresh and exciting. It was delving into some fairly played-out demonic possession/exorcism tropes, with the setting and some of the background details being the only things giving it a slightly unique flavor. Things continued to turn more toward the familiar by the time the film reached its final 30-40 minutes. To say more might be spoiling (and it was fun not knowing exactly what that final act would involve while watching), but while it's sort of entertaining and effectively brutal, it was a little disappointing that it ended feeling less inspired than when it started.In the interest of not being too much of a downer, I still liked more things in The Medium than I disliked. Even with the slower parts, it mostly earned its 2+ hour runtime, and the mockumentary style was honestly done pretty well, too. It felt like it could've been heading somewhere revolutionary, though inevitably didn't... but the ride still proved to be worth taking, and I'd say it was an overall solid horror movie.

It was not scary at all, in mah opinion maybe because i've watched too many horror movies like this so I found this one boring, such a waste of time. Besides that, it was just illogical and dumb :) in some scenes. The climax wasnt good, i expected it to have some plot twist or sth better.However, the acting of the main actress was very impressive :)

I just enjoyed one of the scariest films in recent years. You all should watch if you are a fan of horror films. People with a pessimistic way show that they don't know what a nice horror film is. That's all.

"Medium" is an interesting footage film, it tries to escape a little from the current mediocrity of the genre, using a mockumentary style but fails to innovate and in the end ends up arresting the viewer for its cultural and religious exploration rather than its plot. Weak performances, a script that works well with cultural issues but when it comes to horror, it lacks a lot, has some merits in its direction, especially for the final half of the film, where tapes some fake jump scare to create tension and deflates the tension in others, wasting some of the potential. In the end we have a feature with a different proposal that is actually the same as always, with good ideas, a script that knows how to work with stories and characters but not horror.. 6.5/10.
Yes, The Wailing was damn good horror film. The Medium isn't. Period.

Good cinematography but the scary aspect, where they just acted goofy ruined everything, it didn't felt like a scary scene anymore. The first half, which builds up, it really was good but how they portrayed the supernatural was really amateur, specially when it's from the same guy who made Shutter, he could've relied on showing nothing or kept building the tension without even showing anything, making it more creepy and fearful but the main character's weird possessed acting or whatever it was, ruined it. Would still recommend, still better than most recent horror movies.

It is quite spooky. It starts out very strong then goes rotten toward the end. After some reading, though, I found that this film actually has an enticing storyline (which, to some degree, is open for interpretations). However, production choices are not well executed. For instance, this film is presented as a documentary (mockumentary to be specific) but why is it necessary to add those background experimental music for jump-scare value? NOT AT ALL. Blending documentary-style realism with supernatural terror, The Medium offers a chilling exploration of belief, possession, and the fragile line between faith and fear.This Thai-Korean horror film follows Nim, a shaman in the Isan region, who believes she has inherited a protective spirit. When her niece Mink begins displaying disturbing behavior, what seems at first like spiritual succession quickly unravels into something sinister. Presented through a faux-documentary lens, the film captures both intimate family dynamics and escalating horror with unsettling immediacy.The film excels in its atmosphere. The mockumentary style grounds the narrative in realism, making supernatural events feel disturbingly plausible. The rural Isan setting adds cultural specificity, highlighting how local traditions and spiritual practices coexist with modern skepticism. Performances, especially by Sawanee Utoomma as Nim, are compelling-her restrained yet powerful presence anchors the film's emotional and spiritual weight.The first half is the strongest, with slow-burning tension and thematic depth that explores faith, inheritance, and cultural identity. However, the second half shifts toward more conventional horror, leaning on graphic possession sequences and chaotic pacing. While these moments deliver visceral shocks, they somewhat undercut the subtle dread established earlier.Ultimately, The Medium succeeds as both cultural exploration and horror spectacle. It may feel uneven, but its combination of authenticity and terror makes it stand out in the genre.Rating: 7/10 - A gripping, atmospheric horror film that blends cultural realism with supernatural dread, though its tonal shift weakens the overall impact.

Shot in mockumentary style, The Medium is an intriguing Thai horror film, that starts off as a documentary which is being made about folk magic and local forms of shamanism in the Isan region of the country.The main subject of their documentary has become an adherent to a Goddess named Ba Yan, in order to gain her shamanic abilities.Though, as far as I can tell, Ba Yan is not a real deity in the Thai pantheon.But is probably derived from "Banyan", a sacred form of fig tree, which acts as a common motif in Buddhist mythology- pertaining to a tale in which Gods can live in the trees, and become a benefactor of the person who makes a promise to them, and is able to keep that promise.Although, Bayanism is also an offshoot of the Bahai faith, as well.Both of these readings might be pertinent, in that many forms of Christianity look at them as antagonists of the faith; while the feeling is not necessarily reciprocated in the other direction.Either way, it seems that the family of this particular shaman have inherited their connection to Ba Yan- with the connection being passed down from generation to generation, along the female line.Originally, it was supposed to be her sister that was chosen.However, when she rejected the call- and turned to the Christian faith, to escape her fate- the aunt of our main character was next in line to inherit the honour (or burden, depending on how you look at it).Thus, the plot, here, centers around the calling being passed on to her niece- Mink.At least, that is what we are led to believe at first...Because, as things progress, everything takes a dark turn, when her mother takes her to a random acceptance ceremony- in order to hand her daughter over to the Goddess- she, unwittingly, opens Ming up to be a vessel for all sorts of demonic entities.To understand this, you can look to gnosticism (a form of Christian shamanism)- particularly Valentinus, who describes the mind as being "like an inn, which can be inhabited by many different types of spirits", if given the chance.Which is effectively what ends up happening to Mink...first, driving her toward a life of nymphomania; before progressively pushing her down a path that is much more dark and violent.Eventually, we learn that this is all the fault of Ming's mother and father.Her father, because he had inherited a curse along his familial line, which he passed onto Mink.And her mother, because she refused the call of Ba Yan, which enacted her vengeance toward the family.To appease this...they try all manner of folk remedies, in an attempt to free Mink from her torment.But each of these attempts seem to fail...and make everything much worse.Inevitably pushing the film in a direction you would never expect...Now, I don't want spoil the ending...but it clearly didn't sit well with a significant portion of Western audiences (based on the rhetoric espoused in other reviews).I'm not entirely sure why this is (as it's as good an explanation as any)...but I chock it up to a lack of understanding about shamanism, and folk magic, in general.Either way...this film is totally wild, and awesome, in all the best possible ways.And is- as far as I can tell- one of the best found-footage format horror films ever made.As that is what it effectively what it is.It has everything you want in a great horror film: style, atmosphere, a badass storyline, great acting, twists, misdirection, tits, gore, monsters, and action...all spiced with a little magic!!!So, if you don't leave loving this film...there is clearly something wrong with you.Because it's a damned masterpiece.Who said Christians had a monopoly on the apocalypse?!8.5 out of 10.

Full disclosure: We only watched 1'45" of the 2'10" movie. It was pretty clear how it was going to end by then, and we just couldn't take it any more.This movie is LONG, and unfolds as slowly as The Exorcist, except without the allure. It's not a terrible effort; the acting wasn't bad at all, and the cinematography was nice when they weren't doing the shaky-cam documentary style--but unfortunately that was most of the movie.The main girl is Mink, and boy, does everyone shout "Mink!" a lot in this movie. You could turn it into a drinking game, except that you'd die of alcohol poisoning about seventeen hours into the movie. I would estimate that they say her name no fewer than 250 times during the course of the film.The film offers some nice glimpses into life in the rural Thai countryside. That's about the best I can say for it. The dramatic buildup is far too slow, and by the time it gets to the trope-y horror at the end, you really don't care anymore, and are more or less rooting for them all to die so the movie will be over.There were some unpleasantly abrupt moments in which critically important characters appeared just exactly when they were needed for the plot, with no previous mention of them, making it a bit confusing. (The most obvious one was the baby towards the end, but there were others.)There are some scenes of animal cruelty that could easily be a trigger or turn-off for some viewers; I found them a bit over the top myself.The movie was not scary at any point, although you would probably find it scary if you have literally never watched a horror movie before. On the plus side, there were no jump scares, but on the minus side, there were no other scares either.I really wanted to like this movie. My wife and I love supernatural horror, and we love foreign (especially Asian) horror. We've seen plenty of both Thai and Korean horror movies and series. The Medium, unfortunately, is just not worth watching, even if you're pretty desperate for horror content.

Although "Medium" can be considered opinion-oriented with flakoric and anthropological strains, which is narrated in the context of the horror genre, it is also a character-oriented film about a middle-aged woman named Nim, who has been working as a shaman (the equivalent of our own exorcist) for years. And shares his experiences with a documentary group.In fact, we are facing a hybrid and hybrid film, whose fiction and documentary strains are interwoven and mixed, and basically it has a documentary process, so that it can be considered a fiction documentary as well. Nim lives in a village in Thailand and has a sister who has a daughter named Min. Nim believes that he has been in contact with an ancient and benevolent spirit named Bayan for a long time and owes his prosperity to him. In a ceremony in a temple, strange behavior occurs from Maine, the main character's niece starts an argument with someone who many believe is due to excessive alcohol consumption, but these behaviors gradually become more serious and increase to the point where she is fired from her job.Regardless of the horrible elements that can be traced in the heart of traditions, thoughts and local customs in this story, the space, geography and environmental context of the story also add to the horror of the film. In other words, the forest atmosphere, the quiet rural environments, the silent movement of people in small houses and the fog should be considered as important elements of creating fear in the medium. From the sudden movements of the camera towards a certain creature to accompany the audience with the fear of the character to the creation of a deep connection between many local beliefs of a particular place, they work hand in hand to form a scary story in the medium.The same inflammation and sharp rhythm that exists in the narration of the story engages the audience in the story and does not tire of watching it. The acting of the actors is so believable that they make the audience doubt whether they are really actors or real residents of the same village who are in front of the camera! All these features have helped "Medium" to take advantage of exciting suspense for the narrative and ultimately bring the audience with it, so that the film achieved significant commercial success at the box office and became the sixth highest-grossing film of South Korean cinema in 2021. Assigned to himselfRegardless of the dramatic or entertaining aspects of the film, "Medium" is also significant in terms of anthropology and sociological readings, which can help to understand the underlying layers of culture and religious beliefs in Southeast Asia, especially Thailand."Medium" does not claim to be an innovative narrative in creating a situation of fear, nor does it imitate Hollywood stereotypes of the horror genre. Rather, it formulates and portrays fear in its anthropological representation. The realistic and realistic tone of the film institutionalizes fear here, not as a fantasy, but as a reality built from the lived experience of the native people, and finally a different horror film is created.

The Medium is a Thai mockumentary horror film that follows a shaman/ medium Nim, who takes it upon herself to exorcise the evil spirit possessing her niece. The movie takes an interesting approach to its subject matter by deciding to tell the story through that of a documentary. It helps all the more that the characters are grounded, the lore is local and is heavily tied to the cultural and superstitious roots of the village the story takes place.It's an extremely well made movie that also paces itself quite well to balance out its 130-minute runtime; slowly engrossing us into the lore and thus building upon it with all the storytelling mastery one could expect in this genre. Now sure, it does proceed to write itself into a corner when the final act begins to rely on the overused horror movie trope of human irrationality and stupidity, but at least to me, it never really ruined the overall movie; as I don't see it at all being about its resolution, but more of its build-up. And of course, a better ending could have elevated the movie so much more, but I don't really feel dissatisfied with what I watched.The Medium is a more than competant movie that I really don't mind recommending to fans of the genre. It's an enjoyable work of storytelling that has all the right tools to give us such a great cinematic experience.

The Medium is a Thailand Horror movie taking place in the Isan region of the country and is centred around Shamanism and a family who is going through a possession ordeal. Didn't know anything other than that it is produced and co-written by Na Hong-Jin, a South Korean creative who wrote and directed two great films i.e The Chaser, and The Wailing, the latter of which if you've seen would give you an instant hype boost if one is looking for Horror as it's one of the best Horror films I've seen in recent memory. And thankfully, this movie turned out to be a great fear-inducing creepfest watch.Shot in a found-footage documentary style, the director Banjong Pisanthanakun used that style to its full effect, for the most part, drenching you in the locale and the mythology of shamans, which in it itself was engrossing and kept me hooked from the start and was also necessary since it is a slow burn horror. That style, though, did act as a double-edged sword sometimes as you did have to suspend your disbelief a bit more than usual and also the fact that sometimes the characters would just make questionable or stupid decisions while the filming crew is there with them, but nothing too damning or ruinous.Of course, this movie wouldn't have nearly as much draw and effectiveness if it weren't for its wonderful Thai cast where pretty much everyone gave a good-great performance. Legitimately felt like you're just diving in to their lives and watching them go through this nightmare. Special nod to Narilya Gulmongkolpech who plays Mink, one of the leads who they suspect is possessed. It's her first feature-length film role (from what I can tell) and she was absolutely fantastic and is going places.Now, the movie isn't wholly original when it comes to presenting you the Horror aspects as you'll definitely find cliches and tropes associated with this style of filmmaking but it didn't need to be either as the execution alongside a complete change of the area from usual horror films was enough for full immersion. It also hardly relies on jump scares but instead uses its slow-burn horror and local culture/mythology to slowly sear the experience into your skull. I can think of only one cheap jump scare which I knew was coming and it still got me.Easily one of the best Horror movies of the year and the best found-footage style ones I've seen in recent times. The final 30-minutes or so were just... DAMN! Highly recommended. Just know that, as mentioned above, it is a slow burn, so the pacing isn't fast for a good chunk of the movie but it is of the good kind, the type where tension and intrigue are slowly wound up to a high degree and then is given a proper release in the climax. And if I were to rate it, I'd give it a solid 8/10.

The Medium's choice of going with documentary style adds to that effect as well, even if there are conveniently clear shot of the horror transpired and the movie sometimes deliberately cuts back and forth between several cameras in one sequence to allow natural flow for the audience. The well-placed ending which concludes the movie in a simple statement, further solidifies the main theme and premise of the movie which somehow puts it first within category of a tragedy drama and horror second. But such delivery is not only appropriate to the movie, but also poetical even if full of woe for the characters we observed.

Right, well granted I am not well-traversed in the Thai folklore with shaman and possessions, so I was somewhat at a loss here with this movie. But it being a Thai horror movie that I hadn't already seen, then of course I jumped at the chance to sit down and watch it here in 2022.I wasn't having any expectations at all to writers Chantavit Dhanasevi, Na Hong-jin, Banjong Pisanthanakun or Siwawut Sewatanon. So the slate was clean and they had all the opportunities to impress me with "The Medium".First of all, I was by no means impressed by the documentary-style type of filming that they opted for in this movie. I mean, a shaky camera that is all over the place, just doesn't cut it for me. When I sit down to watch a movie, I want proper cinematography and not something I could have filmed myself with my own digital camera. And then the pacing of the storyline was just atrociously slow paced, which suffocated the fun right out of the movie.Running at over 2 hours long, "The Medium" is a slow and monotonous affair to get through, especially since it takes director Banjong Pisanthanakun forever to set the stage and build up the atmosphere. And by the time the stage is set, then I was essentially ready to disembark the movie. You need to go well into more than half of the run time before things start to pick up, and by then it it just too little, too late. And the last 15 or 20 minutes of the movie was just utter rubbish.It should be said that "The Medium" definitely have some good and solid acting performances by the cast ensemble, but especially Narilya Gulmongkolpech (playing Mink) and Sawanee Utoomma (playing Nim) stands out with their performances.For a horror movie, then the movie was frightfully devoid of anything scary. Perhaps being a life-long fan of horror have hardened and seasoned me, because I didn't find anything scary about "The Medium". Well, aside from the slow pacing of the story. I suppose you need to be a Thai or have knowledge of the Thai superstitions to find anything scary here.If you enjoy Thai horror movies, then "The Medium" is not a movie I would recommend you waste 130 minutes on watching. It just simply doesn't cut it.My rating of "The Medium" lands on a very generous four out of ten stars.

The last time I felt such dread, such inquisitive curiosity about what was going on, and felt desperate at each and every twist of the plot, was when I watched Noroi for the first time. Ever since, only a few selected horror films have managed to evoke such feelings. I am glad to say that The Medium absolutely nailed every important aspect, and it was a rewarding, dreadful experience that creeps on you slowly.Direct by the creator of Shutter, you can start to get an idea about the style of the film and the ambience it tries to achieve. It captures masterfully the rural life on a low-class family in Thailand, showcasing the beauty and connection of the family living in a forsaken town in the middle of a mountain valley, as well as the rituals and customs they partake in. Like a proper found-footage, the narrative is structured in a way that feels grounded and realistic to the audience; in no moment are you truly pulled out of the experience from sudden jumpscares or silly turns. Each seconds feels carefully crafted to immerse you in the story and feel the stakes slowly grow.When I compared this film to Noroi, I did so both as a very accurate representation of what the film is, and how well it executes its story by creating a fantastically creepy plot that involves rituals and shamans. It feels like a mystery film at times, showing you the clues but leaving just enough for the imagination. The editing asks you to stay still and pay attention, but it rewards you greatly.The performances are very heartfelt and touching. The pain and sadness is captured really well as well as the fear that they experience. At no time did this feel amateurish or cheap.Despite being rather long for your average horror movie, The Medium uses every minute well. At no point did I feel bored or like I was wasting my time. Maybe if you prefer very fast-paced movies then you won't enjoy it as much, but if you are a fan of found-footage and Asian horror, this one is a must.

I initially believed it to be a documentary with actual people and a true narrative, but I subsequently realised it was a fictitious film due of the graphic violence, inappropriate sexual material, abuses, and cannibalism.A family in Thailand's Isan area is the subject of the narrative. Nim (medium/shaman) claimed to have been transmitted down the centuries by a local divinity named Ba Yan. Her younger sister Nim steps in for her older sister Noi, who was selected to host Ba Yan's soul but declined.A family in Thailand's Isan area is the subject of the narrative. Nim have claimed to have claimed to be possessed and has passed down the centuries by a local goddess named Ba Yan. Nim steps in for her younger sister Noi, when Ban Yan selects her his spirit to host.FIRST THOUGHTS: You can only imagine what a powerful film this is if you believe me when I explain that it is fictional by God's grace. The reason I started this review with "This movie deserved an Oscar" is that the amount of work that each actor put into portraying their characters is phenomenal. The film's directing, as well as the staging, lighting, narrative, and cinematography.DIRECTION: Since the director of this film is the same as that of The Wailing, I cannot even question his originality in making it. Despite being a fiction, this documentary makes you feel uneasy and ask yourself "really, is it the fiction? Why did it seem real?" His ability to see the Thai culture clearly painted for us a picture of greed, the boundaries of what one may believe, materialism, hope, and survival.CHARACTERS/ACTORS: There are graphic possession moments that were shot in a documentary style, so you can only imagine how genuine they must have felt to see. Actors devoted themselves to their roles as they were their only source of income for their mortgage, rent, and food. They performed it so well , which gave viewers the impression that it's all real. It's incredibly realistic and natural. I wonder how much dedication and effort went into making this movie. Most significantly, the actress who portrayed Mink did a fantastic job.PLOTLINE: The storyline naturally pleases your interest in finding out more information about the topics covered in the film. The viewer's feelings are maintained throughout the whole film through a few specific scenes and, more importantly, by dialogue that is left hanging with incomplete facial expressions. Excellent decision! Because everything was interconnected, I didn't feel any scenes were unnecessary.I recommend this film to any aspiring horror critics since it is entertaining and lends itself to a number of intriguing theories. I guarantee you won't look back on it with regret.

The Thai film «Mediumship» (also known as "The Medium") has a splendid first hour: like a serious ethnographic documentary, it approaches the concept of "spirit" in Thai culture, through Nim, a shaman of the goddess Ba Yan, who informs us that, for Thais, the spirit is not an exclusive patrimony of humanity but manifests itself in all the components of the Universe. With a pleasant personality and strong beliefs, Nim will venture into a case of possession in the middle of a family that drags a macabre history of incest, genocide, and labor exploitation.As the film progresses, we discover that «Mediumship» is a fake documentary, with actors who assume their roles naturally in front of the camera. However, the problem begins when the movie is defined as a horror film. The genre is the least important, but horror told as a fake documentary has given few satisfactory results.I only remember examples from the last few decades. The best attempt for me was a drama called «Cloverfield» (2008) and the least successful, «The Blair Witch Project» (1999). In my case, all suspension of disbelief disappears when I realize that it is quite unlikely that a person (including professional cameramen) would remain filming behind a camera during moments of supreme physical or psychological threat, especially of a supernatural nature. The documentary approach is then plagued by foolish or clumsy explanations to justify the presence of cameras in the middle of the action.To give the film the death blow, the scriptwriters had the unfortunate idea of removing the shaman from the plot in the last 30 minutes. To please audiences addicted to violent and bloody horror films, Nim's logic and restraint were replaced by a feast of blood and screams in a mix of cannibalism, acrobatics and pyrotechnics. I said to myself "I pass," but it was too late.P. S. But I would not tell anyone "Do not watch it." There is no accounting for taste!

"The Medium," a 2021 Thai-South Korean found footage supernatural horror film directed by Banjong Pisanthanakun and produced by Na Hong-jin, presents a chilling and thought-provoking exploration of faith, possession, and the blurred lines between belief and exploitation. The film unfolds through the lens of a documentary crew following Nim (Sawanee Utoomma), a shaman in the Isan region of Thailand, who is believed to be the successor to the spirit of Ba Yan.The initial premise is seemingly straightforward: to document the daily life and rituals of a local shaman. However, the narrative takes a dark and disturbing turn as Nim's niece, Mink (Narilya Gulmongkolpech), begins to exhibit increasingly erratic and unsettling behavior, suggesting she might be the next in line to inherit the shamanic spirit. What starts as an observation of traditional spiritual practices gradually descends into a terrifying account of potential demonic possession.The film's strength lies in its slow-burn approach, meticulously building an atmosphere of unease and dread. The found footage style, while a familiar trope in horror, is employed effectively here, lending a sense of realism and immediacy to the increasingly disturbing events. The camera becomes the audience's eye, intimately witnessing Mink's gradual descent into what appears to be a terrifying battle for her soul.Sawanee Utoomma delivers a compelling and nuanced performance as Nim, portraying a woman deeply connected to her spiritual traditions yet increasingly troubled by the unfolding events within her family. Narilya Gulmongkolpech's portrayal of Mink is particularly harrowing, capturing the character's vulnerability and the horrifying transformations she undergoes. Her performance is central to the film's impact, conveying the sheer terror and helplessness of potential possession.Banjong Pisanthanakun masterfully crafts a sense of cultural immersion, depicting the rituals, beliefs, and superstitions prevalent in the rural Thai setting. The film doesn't shy away from depicting the visceral and often unsettling aspects of these practices, blurring the lines between genuine spiritual connection and potential manipulation. This cultural backdrop adds a layer of authenticity and intrigue to the horror elements.As the film progresses, the initial documentary objective unravels, and the crew becomes increasingly entangled in the terrifying events they are documenting. The ambiguity surrounding the nature of the possessing entity - whether it is a benevolent ancestral spirit, a malevolent force, or something else entirely - adds to the film's unsettling atmosphere. The film subtly raises questions about the nature of faith, the power of belief, and the potential for both good and evil within spiritual practices.However, "The Medium" is not without its criticisms. Some viewers found the pacing slow in the initial stages, with the true horror escalating more significantly in the latter half. The found footage style, while effective for creating realism, can also be disorienting for some viewers. Additionally, the film's intense and graphic depictions of potential possession and violence in the final act can be disturbing and may not be suitable for all audiences.Despite these points, "The Medium" stands out as a compelling and unsettling horror film that transcends typical genre tropes. It delves into complex themes of faith, family curses, and the vulnerability of the human spirit. The film's unsettling atmosphere, strong performances, and thought-provoking exploration of cultural beliefs make it a memorable and disturbing cinematic experience that lingers long after the credits roll, prompting reflection on the unseen forces that might shape our lives and the terrifying possibilities that lie within the realm of the spiritual.

I've raved about mockumentaries before. I love them, especially horror mockumentaries. They almost always have that higher level of skill and effort that most found footage films don't have. Exactly the case with The Medium, which allows Thailand's spiritual side to build the story up, characters and all, turning everything into something that almost seems like a mashup of American demonic and Japanese ghost girl horror. It really is quite a treat to watch from beginning to end.The characters are genuinely intriguing, speaking volumes of the writing. They're all believable, almost to the point where they come off as too real. Narilya Gulmongkolpech (Mink) and Sawanee Utoomma (Nim) are the main drivers here (especially the creepier scenes featuring Narilya's brilliant creepy performances), but there's an overall excellence to each performance that elevates both the sinister and non-sinister elements at play. The previously mentioned Thai spiritualism makes the possession horror content different, though also familiar, blending horror tropes from American demon horror and Japanese ghost horror together to form very pleasing and welcome surprise. But perhaps most fascinating is the way the camera work is executed here. While it does lean more towards a found footage POV approach, it also intentionally makes the viewer a silent participant, echoing how a POV-set videogame would make you feel during a cutscene. It has this heightened realism to it, which is only further enhanced by the focus on a practical approach that also comes off as higher-than-usual-budget. The Medium gets a ton of points for that, as I'm personally a big fan of excellently executed visual work.The sound, more specifically the bits of inserted music, was a bit of a turn off. I get it, it's meant to add to the atmosphere and tone, but some choice additions felt unnecessary, almost edging into hokey territory though thankfully being pulled back enough to avoid ruining more critical scenes. I did love the crisp sound detail, especially for the more harrowing moments, including one that I knew was going to happen but still gasped at when it actually happened. You'll know it when you see it.It's been a while since I've enjoyed a great horror mockumentary, and I'm glad it's The Medium that brought that enjoyment. It's a great horror mockumentary with lots of creepy and sometimes disturbing content. Highly Recommended.Adios.

The Medium is the perfect film if you want to engage with Thai culture and religion under the auspices of a horror movie.Pro
-The acting is so natural and authentic that you'll immediately forget that this is not an actual documentary featuring real people.-It's honestly fascinating as a fictional exploration of shamanism and folk religion.Cons
-Easily could have been 45 min shorter.-There is a real sense here that western horror tropes were sort of just stapled onto this story as an afterthought and they definitely don't fit.-The ending is a real letdown - it doesn't make sense to build up for two hours to this showdown if there was no hope of winning either way.Watch it if it's free and you're interested in Thai folk religion - otherwise probably avoid it.

If you see this, please, watch the movie and judge for yourself. Many people prefer mediocre American crap predictable horror movies. This one has a good beginning, an amazing mid and an insane ... literally insane ending that will make you think about the movie days later.From the opening scene of The Medium, I was hooked. The atmosphere was eerie and unsettling, setting the tone for the rest of the film. The characters were well-developed and the acting was top-notch. The story itself was unique and kept me on the edge of my seat throughout. As the plot unfolded, I found myself increasingly invested in the protagonist's journey and eager to see how it would all unfold.The middle of the movie took a dark and twisted turn, leading to a series of shocking revelations that left me reeling. The tension continued to build as the protagonist's sanity seemed to unravel before my eyes. The cinematography and sound design added to the overall sense of unease, creating a truly immersive experience.And then came the ending. Without giving too much away, I can say that it was unlike anything I had ever seen before. It was bold, unexpected, and left me with more questions than answers. It forced me to reconsider everything I thought I knew about the film and left me wanting to watch it again just to pick up on all the subtle hints and foreshadowing that I may have missed the first time around.In a genre filled with cliches and jump scares, The Medium stood out as a breath of fresh air. It was a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant film that stayed with me long after the credits had rolled. I found myself mulling over its themes and imagery for days, trying to decipher its deeper meaning and unravel its mysteries.So, to those who may be skeptical of this movie based on its reviews, I urge you to give it a chance. The Medium is a truly exceptional film that deserves to be seen and appreciated for its originality and craftsmanship. It may not be for everyone, but for those who appreciate a well-crafted and thought-provoking horror film, it is sure to leave a lasting impression.

The Medium is a fascinating and immersive film that drags the audience deep into the world of spiritual practitioners, where the laws of cause and effect run their unavoidable course. It brilliantly portrays the Isan region not just as a setting, but as a place where ancient, unseen forces dictate the lives of the living.The most striking aspect of the movie is how it challenges our assumptions about spiritual devotion. It suggests a grim reality: when we devote ourselves to a powerful astral entity, we might discover too late that there is always something stronger and more malevolent lurking in the shadows. Instead of finding a path to spiritual enlightenment, the characters find themselves reduced to mere pawns-messengers or servants in a cosmic battle that only serves to satisfy the dark intentions of the entity itself.The tragedy is made even more profound by the shaman's final confession of doubt. When Nim, the veteran medium, admits that she never truly felt the presence of the Goddess she served, it shatters the last remaining hope for the family. This moment of spiritual "blindness" makes the ending feel inevitable and terrifyingly bleak. It highlights that once you are caught in the web of these entities, your personal faith may not be enough to save you if the "Goddess" you rely on was never really there to begin with.The documentary-style cinematography makes the experience feel raw and authentic, pulling you into the family's desperation. It is a sobering look at how faith can be twisted and how "serving a goddess" can easily become a nightmare of possession and destruction. It's not just a horror movie; it's a warning about the true cost of opening doors to the spiritual world without knowing what is actually waiting on the other side.Verdict: A masterclass in folk horror. It is unsettling, thought-provoking, and deeply tragic, proving that in the realm of the spirits, humans are often just collateral damage.

If he didn't match the horoscopes with his soulmate in time, he would have life threatening problems. The person who would be his soulmate must not be a woman, not born in Phra Nakhon. The age must not have the remainder of one At first. If they survive, they will survive together. If they are in danger, they will be in danger together. Apart from living a better life since Saengrawee moved to Sittikornkan castle, he sensed some mysterious power and he had nightmares like never before. He was also haunted by the spirit of a woman endlessly Saengrawee could feel spiteful like he would be assassinated. However, all strange events or feelings rarely happened when Saengrawee was with Phra Ploeng. Their feelings began to change and develop as days and months passed by, but the barriers to love remained. Saengrawee had been attacked by evil spirits many times. Series of strange events began to worry Phra Ploeng, who secretly fell for Saengrawee. Phra Ploeng swore to himself that... He would never let anyone harm Saengrawee ever again... title: Ploy

A violent death of a relative brings Wit and his wife, Dang, back to Bangkok from America, where they own a Thai restaurant, for the first time in 7 years. As soon as they arrive in Bangkok at 5.30 am. Wit and Dang check into a five star hotel downtown. Wit finds out that he is out of cigarettes once they are inside the room. He goes down to the lobby bar. After getting his pack of cigarette from the bartender Wit decides to order a cup of coffee and smoke his cigarette there. The girl from the table in the dark corner comes to Wit to ask if she could borrow his lighter. Wit hands her his lighter. Then she asks if she could borrow one cigarette too. The girl sits down and lights up one of his cigarettes and they somehow strike up a conversation. Wit learns that her name is PLOY. This is how our little tale of love and jealousy begins. A highly detailed psychological drama with three strangers locked inside one hotel room. It starts with subtle suspicions and builds up to hilarious jealousy, as the appearance of the young woman triggers the couple to suddenly realize how they had grown apart in their seven year marriage, before reaching a devastating climax. In the final act, the couple is faced with the choice of going separate ways or turns around and embraces each other for a new beginning.

synopsis: In the future, an unseen leader transforms Thailand into a strange world where humans are forbidden from touching. Part political essay, part erotic gay drama,.

title: Phii khon pen
synopsis: An actress hired to reenact a beauty queen's murder develops an unexplainable supernatural link with the victim's spirit, leading her to investigate the unsolved crime.

title: May Who?
synopsis: Super standard girl in school is on a quest to win the love of a school senior heart throbber with her new found friend. The only secret is that she can discharge electricity when she gets excited.

title: Bang Rajan
synopsis: Set right before the fall of Thailand's old capital, Ayuttaya, Bang Rajan draws on the legend of a village of fighters who bravely fended off the Burmese armies.

title: 7 Days
synopsis: A man woke up in different bodies every morning without any memory. He has no idea what and why this happened. All his need is to be back to normal and apologize to his girlfriend.

title: Tears of the Black Tiger
synopsis: With its loud acting style, exuberant sets and stunning shots in pastel colours, this Thai cult film is as much a parody as an homage to the Western and the romantic tearjerker.

title: 3 A.M. 3D
synopsis: Thailand's latest horror omnibus is made up of three chilling stories. Two sisters who own a wig shop.

title: Halabala
synopsis: Inspector Dan leads the team of infirm police officers to hunt down the brutal escaped prisoner in the Halabala Forest down south of Thailand, only to discover that the dark secret inside the forest is turning against them.

title: The Giant King
synopsis: Zork and Pinky, sworn enemies, wake up chained to each other with no memory. In search of answers, they wander the barren wasteland, looking for RAM, the creator of all robots.

title: Mekong Hotel
synopsis: Shifting between fact and fiction in a hotel situated along the Mekong River, a film maker rehearses a movie expressing the bonds between a vampiric mother and daughter.

title: Tootsies & the Fake
synopsis: Make way. 3 tootsies, 1 lesbian, and an A list superstar are coming. Get ready for their new adventures.

title: A Gift
synopsis: Three different love stories are linked together, and based on the music composed by King Bhumibol

title: The Beast Below
synopsis: A once famous singer enters a hometown drilling contest, seeking a cash prize. But a mysterious beast lurks underground, unknown to the organizers.

title: Will You Marry Monk?
synopsis: A Thai monk heads to his sister's wedding in Japan, but grows concerned when he learns about her groom's dark past. As he tries to prevent their union, the former gangster must demonstrate he's truly changed.

title: Under Parallel Skies
synopsis: A man struggling with a painful past tries to move forward, only to discover that the woman in his present life has an uncanny connection to his past.

title: 2gether: The Movie
synopsis: Tine wants to get rid of a gay admirer so he finds a fake boyfriend: Sarawat. The two become close and intense emotions soon erupt. As Tine and Sarawat enter the second year of their relationship.

title: Necromancer 2020
synopsis: Win has to master powerful sorcery to seek revenge against the people who attacked him for his father's amulet. However, a satanic cult gets in his way and corrupts his girlfriend's mind.

title: The Teacher's Diary
synopsis: A teacher arrives at a rural school and falls in love with his predecessor by reading her diary.

title: ATM: Er Rak Error
synopsis: Two enamored employees in a bank with no fraternization policy must recover their company's lost money while trying to keep their relationship a secret.

title: Hope Frozen
synopsis: After her untimely death, a scientist from Bangkok cryo preserves his daughter's brain. Scandal swirls around the family as they struggle to grieve a child that, in their view, is suspended between death and reawakening.

title: Vengeance of an Assassin
synopsis: The Assassins' Code   Stick to the mission. Never take your eyes off the target. Show no mercy. Natee (Dan Chupong) became a killer for one reason  to discover who killed his parents. As he gets closer to uncovering a secret network of power and corruption, he's double crossed on a job, making him a target and putting everyone he loves in danger. Betrayed, exposed, and hunted by the deadliest killers in the business, now Natee has a new code. Be faster. Stronger. Hit harder. Survive. Director, fight choreographer of ONG BAK and mentor to action star Tony Jaa, Panna Rittikrai reunites with Dan Chupong of BORN TO FIGHT (2004) in his final film.

title: Moments of Love
synopsis: My Lovely Tutor: When nineteen year old Pun has to repeat grade twelve, his parents hire handsome fourth year university student Get to tutor him. However, Pun's after love rather than knowledge. My Ex Boyfriend: At the end of high school, Forth tells his close friend Non that he loves him before Non's ready. Forth accepts the heartbreak. When Non enters university, though, he begins to know himself better and goes to confess to his old friend Forth. However, Forth's own heart has changed. My Heartless Boy: Fort is an extra persistently auditioning for bigger roles and never booking them. Fortunately, he has Pie always waiting by his side to encourage him. Despite this, Fort, who's heartbroken by both his ex and disappointed hopes, doesn't seem to love Pie as Pie does. My Crazy Romance: The two meet in a tumultuous transition period of James' life. Smart tries everything to make James feel better about himself, but James is stuck in his suffering. Smart can do nothing but increase his efforts.

title: Timeline
synopsis: Mat a mother forced to raise her son Tan on her own after being widowed early in her marriage. In this Mat gets help from Watt, who falls in love with her for long time. Tan is expected to be like his dad but instead wants to escape what he regards as the narrow confines of his mother's world. His dreams look like coming true when he meets June, a free spirit who knows what she wants from life. The young woman quickly makes up for what Tan feels he's missing and in the process helps him reconnect with his mother.

title: Buppha Rahtree
synopsis: A shy college girl in Bangkok catches the attention of several male classmates who make a cruel bet about her, leading to unexpected and haunting consequences.

title: Hong hun
synopsis: Directed by Kulp Kaljareuk, this modern adaptation of a classic horror tale revolves around two people whose loved ones die after they get a wax figure shaped like themselves. An investigation into the deaths brings the two together as they seek the truth behind the mystery.

title: Pee Nak 2
synopsis: Though they've fulfilled their pledges, First and Balloon secretly leave monkhood so they can live secular lives but a new ghost starts haunting them.

title: Khang paed
synopsis: Each and all of us have to undergo the same life cycle: being born, growing up, and leading the chosen course of life until the end of our time on this world.

title: Die Tomorrow
synopsis: An anthology of short stories about the last day of people's lives inspired by newspaper headlines from 2012 2016.

title: Krai Thong
synopsis: This film tells the legendary tale of hero Krai Thong, who used his extreme force, strength of will and superhuman skills when entering a battle to confront the largest crocodile in the world. This fierce monster, Chalawan, has the power of turning into a human being when he enters his golden cave. Chalawan, in human guise, went into town one day and was utterly captivated by the daughter of a millionaire, Tapaokaew, and kidnapped her, returning with her to his cave. Her father, distressed by his daughter's disappearance, made an announcement that anyone strong enough to kill the legendary Chalawan would get as a prize his daughter, and a lot of money. Krai Thong knew this was a job for him.

title: E Sarn Zombie
synopsis: Itt becomes a supermarket manager. This leads him to meet Tonnun, an employee who exhibits strange and mysterious behaviour. She often steals expired fresh meat from the supermarket, making the manager suspicious. He needs to find out why.

title: Dark World
synopsis: The end of the Third World War resulted in the collapse of the world's economies; humans live without law. The rich are like gods, while the poor struggle as slaves. Three poor girls find themselves in a game where the losers die.

title: Where We Belong
synopsis: Sue, the crazy girl that feels as if she was born in the wrong place. But the craziest thing she's ever done is that she is about to leave everything behind, including Belle.
Rainbow has just moved to an international school in Phuket, in Southern Thailand.

title: Patong Girl
synopsis: Young German Boy on holiday falls in love with beautiful thai girl. Movie is a nice little gem with a twist.

title: My Precious
synopsis: Tong and his group of friends are in love with the same girl, Lin. Tong is forced to be supervised by another student due to his bad behavior. And his school life changes learning, playing and finding the first love.

title: Cracked
synopsis: Ruja inherited the painting from her deceased father and hired Tim, an art restorer to repair it, but they don't know that this invaluable art came with invaluable horror.

title: Mummys Island
synopsis: A young man trained in magic by his grandfather embarks on a quest to find his mermaid mother's missing husband. Armed with mystical weapons, he battles monsters while protecting an ancient kingdom.

title: Ghost Ship
synopsis: At a dark pier in the middle of the night, a boat captain and his mate, Nong, are readying their vessel for the next trip. But what they discover is shocking: the lifeless body of Mia, the wife of the boat's owner, is hanged from a mast in a gruesome fashion. The corpse also sets off panic among other sailors. The captain orders everyone to calm down. He decides that he has to get rid of the body, and comes up with a plan to throw Mia's body in the middle of the sea. But it's not that simple. Once the ship sets sail, the body hidden in the engine room disappears. Mia's spirit is set loose and wreaking havoc on the boat in the middle of the sea. The ghost terrorizes the sailors, who can't escape anywhere except into the water that surrounds them. Things get worse when a storm hits. The only way to save the boat and everyone on it is to locate Mia's body. But there's a more serious question, that no one remembers to ask: Who murdered Mia?
A young location scout meets the art director of her project in a day they will keep in their memories for a while, each for their own reasons.

title: Ta Khon
synopsis: Joy and his friend searched for clues to the mysterious death of his grandmother, which could be linked to the folk tradition known as 'Phi Ta Khon'.

title: Bangkok Love Story
synopsis: An informant and a hit man find themselves passionately entwined after double crossing their crime lord employers.

title: The Cursed Land
synopsis: A widower and his daughter travel's to Thailand's deep south to seek help from a Muslim doctor after unleashing a djinn in a rundown house.

title: Evil
synopsis: After losing both her parents in a horrific tragedy, a young girl ends up with her aunt, a printing house owner and a part time spiritual medium.

title: Nymph
synopsis: An urban husband and wife travel to the jungle and learn just how precious their relationship is.

title: Gagee
synopsis: A period drama set in the city of Varanasi. The king of Varanasi is unable to satisfy his younger wife's sexual needs so she has an affair with one of the king's generals.

title: Cherm
synopsis: Moon faced Sombat, a middle aged taxi driver, usually works the night shift in Bangkok. He is an old fashioned "straight arrow" and the greatest enjoyment in his lonely life is to listen to old Thai songs and Thai classical music late at night on AM radio. One evening a kindred spirit, Nual, a young and very pretty massage parlour girl, enters his cab at midnight after finishing her shift. She makes a deal with him to give her regular rides to work, but their relationship soon becomes more of a friendship. He takes her to his favorite noodle shop to eat, and she takes him to McDonalds for his first ever burger. He then takes her to his favorite dance hall where they watch older couples dance to oldies, and she takes him shopping in a glitzy mall where she reveals her dream of owning a bridal shop. Sombat has written several letters to his favorite DJ expressing his appreciation for the programming and the DJ's friendly patter with the fond wish that one will be read on the air. He muses how he and Nual perform similar services for clients, helping them reach their destinations then continuing on their way. When listening to radio soap operas during day shifts, he visualizes himself and Nual as characters in old Thai movies confronting the roadblocks to love as he daydreams through the shows. Attempting to find a way to finance the bridal shop, he loses all his money in a fraudulent marketing scheme. His own life has begun to parallel a melodrama, with troubles on a par with the exaggerated fictional plots taking over his existence.

title: Kitty the Killer
synopsis: A highly trained teenage assassin, Dina, and her mentor, Charlie, form an unlikely duo as they unexpectedly join forces to stop a sinister plot and save millions of lives.

title: Sin Sisters
synopsis: After graduation from university, childhood friends Ann, Joy, Koi, Mam and Joom move on to follow their respective career paths. They reunite again at a friend's funeral, after which all the five young women decide to stay overnight at Joom's place to recall their good old days. When Ann raises the topic of sex, the conversation goes deeper and deeper until each is forced to reveal details of their most embarrassing sexual experiences   the moments they harbor the most guilt over.

title: Haunted Universities 2nd Semester
synopsis: Every campus has its own horror tales. There's an endless supply of ghost stories passed down from class to class, and three of the scariest tales will be told this time: The "C" Bed, The Final Year's Cheer and The Old Science Building.

title: Suddenly Twenty
synopsis: An annoying granny's suddenly 50 years younger. She gets an Audrey Hepburn look and starts singing again. Her family doesn't recognize her.

title: Prison Fighters: Five Rounds to Freedom
synopsis: After seven years in a Thai prison, a former Muay Thai champion joins a controversial government program that allows inmates to fight for their freedom. A victory in his final fight will grant him a royal pardon and bring him one step closer to the son he left behind.

title: Reincarnate
synopsis: A teacher and his student go on a trip to a magical island where there is urban life and tourist attractions as well as a palace and temples. A haunting past still gnaws, spreads, mates and mutates in a loop that cannot be eliminated. It dissolves and mixes with memories affecting the present and possessing a power that can destroy the future. In this vague atmosphere, the place slowly becomes deserted like a nightmare you want to wake from but cannot resist.

title: Rap nawng sayawng khwan
synopsis: A big group of freshman students go out of town. On the journey, their bus has to cross a creaky old river bridge which is the only way to get to the center of a dark forest. When the bus is halfway across, the bridge collapses and the bus falls deep into the river more than 50 meters from the surface. Nearly all the students are killed. The remaining students walk into the forest until they discover a mysterious, abandoned town. The students are cruelly murdered one by one. Only the survivor will be able to explain it all.

title: Long Weekend
synopsis: The girl Nam befriends the bullied boy Thongsook at the same room in the hospital and she tells that she likes horror films. Thongsook asks whether she would like to see ghosts and he removes his necklace with an amulet and is attacked by ghosts. Years later, Thongsook is an outcast teenager that studies in the same class of Nam and has a crush on her. When Nam and her friends Boy, Jack and the lesbians Beam and Pui decide to spend a night in an infamous island, they do not tell Thongsook. The boatman warns the group that the place is cursed and they should neither stay there nor visit the sanctuary where a tragedy happened but they do not pay attention to his words. Meanwhile Thongsook finds their map and meets his mates in the island. Boy, Jack and Beam force Thongsook to go with them to the sanctuary and he tells that the place is evil. However Boy and Jack take his amulet and lock him up in a cell to scare him but they can not open the padlock.
